name: inteGraality
description: Property-coverage dashboard bot for Wikidata and Wikimedia projects. Reads dashboard configuration templates from MediaWiki, runs SPARQL coverage queries against WDQS or QLever, and writes generated wikitext tables back to the wiki.

nodes.name: Wiki Editor
nodes.description: A Wikidata/Wikimedia editor who manages Property dashboard templates on wiki pages.

nodes.name: MediaWiki
nodes.description: The target MediaWiki instance: www.wikidata.org, commons.wikimedia.org, or meta.wikimedia.org.

nodes.name: QLever
nodes.description: Alternative SPARQL backend (qlever.dev). Used for dashboards that opt in and forced for all Commons pages.

nodes.name: inteGraality Web
nodes.description: Flask HTTP layer: routes, SSE streaming, drill-down query endpoint, and the runs/dashboards browse UI. Triggers processing on demand.

nodes.name: inteGraality Core
nodes.description: Shared Python processing engine invoked by both the web layer and the cron job. Assembles column and grouping configurations from dashboard templates. Always acts as the same pywikibot bot user regardless of trigger.

nodes.name: Toolforge Cron Job
nodes.description: Toolforge scheduled job for full-wiki dashboard refreshes (hundreds of pages per run).

nodes.name: Toolforge Redis
nodes.description: Optional Toolforge-managed Redis PaaS. A cache miss falls back to MediaWiki; never blocks operation.

nodes.name: ToolsDB
nodes.description: Toolforge-managed MariaDB hosting the inteGraality operational schema: wiki and dashboard registry, configuration history with per-column detail, and per-run coverage statistics including per-cell counts.

nodes.name: inteGraality Application
nodes.description: The inteGraality application as a whole: Flask web service and shared Python processing core, deployed together on Toolforge.

nodes.name: Wikimedia Toolforge
nodes.description: Wikimedia's hosting platform for community tools. Runs the web service uWSGI and cron jobs.

relationships.description: Wiki editor submits a single-page dashboard update request via /update.
Wiki editor calls /queries to retrieve the SPARQL queries behind a specific coverage cell.
Wiki editor places or modifies the Property dashboard template on a MediaWiki page.
Web layer spawns a thread invoking the processing engine when an update is requested.
Cron job directly invokes the processing engine for a scheduled full-wiki run, processing all registered dashboards − hundreds of pages.
Processing engine reads dashboard configuration from MediaWiki via pywikibot.
Processing engine writes the generated wikitext coverage table back to MediaWiki via pywikibot, using the same bot user regardless of trigger.
Processing engine executes SPARQL coverage queries against WDQS − default backend.
Processing engine executes SPARQL coverage queries against QLever for Commons dashboards or opt-in dashboards.

Processing engine caches parsed dashboard configs in Redis. On query generation, the cache is read first and MediaWiki only hit on a miss; on update, the cache entry is purged to ensure freshness. Optional — missing Redis does not block operation.
Processing engine writes run results, per-cell coverage counts, and dashboard configuration snapshots to ToolsDB.
Web layer reads entity labels from Redis cache; warms the cache via MediaWiki on a miss.
Web layer reads run history, dashboard registry, and configuration data from ToolsDB to serve the browse UI.
The inteGraality application is composed of its web service and a shared processing core.
Components owned and deployed by inteGraality on Wikimedia Toolforge.
Toolforge-managed PaaS services consumed by inteGraality but operated by the Toolforge platform.

flows.name: Drill-down Query Generation
flows.description: A wiki editor requests the SPARQL queries behind a specific coverage cell. The web layer reads the page config and returns the query URLs; the editor opens them in their browser directly against WDQS or QLever − that execution is outside this system's scope.

transitions.description: Editor calls /queries with page, column, and grouping parameters
Web layer calls core to build the stats object for the page
Core reads the dashboard config from MediaWiki

flows.name: Web-triggered Dashboard Update
flows.description: An editor requests a refresh of a single dashboard page via the web UI; the processing engine reads its config, runs SPARQL queries, and writes the updated table back.

transitions.description: Core fetches and parses the Property dashboard template
SPARQL queries compute per-property, per-grouping coverage counts
Core writes the generated wikitext table back to the wiki page
Core records run results in ToolsDB

flows.name: Scheduled Dashboard Update
flows.description: Toolforge cron job runs a full-wiki refresh, iterating over all registered dashboards − hundreds of pages; same per-page processing path as the web trigger, no HTTP layer involved.

transitions.description: Cron job invokes the processing engine
Core fetches and parses each dashboard's template
Core writes the generated wikitext table back to the wiki page
Core records run results in ToolsDB
